purpose: Research-only evidence packet for five consecutive, individually registered Dublin City NIAH candidates selected from the latest official missing-registration queue.

official_dataset_reference.title: NIAH Data Download
official_dataset_reference.coordinate_note: National CSV ITM values are EPSG:2157; CSV latitude/longitude are separate. Raw coordinate pairs displayed on individual pages are preserved separately because the page display does not label their CRS.

candidate_records.name: Central Model School
candidate_records.description_summary: Detached gable-fronted chapel, built c.1800, with pitched slate roof, red brick walls and pilasters, broken-base pediment, timber sliding sash windows, round-headed entrance and quadripartite glazed fanlight.
candidate_records.appraisal_summary: NIAH notes surviving timber sash windows and red-brick detailing; the building is sited within the former National Model Schools campus.
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact registration 50010226 present in workflow #1987 Dublin City missing-registration queue.

candidate_records.description_summary: Attached square-plan single-bay single-storey granite gate lodge, built c.1838, with granite quoins, moulded cornice, Doric columns, glazed panel and adjoining granite gateway with cast-iron gates.
candidate_records.appraisal_summary: NIAH describes it as one of a pair of gate lodges flanking the railings before the former National Model Schools campus; probably designed by Jacob Owen.
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact registration 50010227 present in workflow #1987 Dublin City missing-registration queue.

candidate_records.name: Saint Mary's Catholic Pro-Cathedral
candidate_records.address: Marlborough Street / Cathedral Street, Dublin 1, Ireland
candidate_records.description_summary: Freestanding stone-built Greek Revival Catholic cathedral, built 1814–1825 on a cruciform plan, with a Portland stone Greek Doric portico, copper-clad dome, granite ashlar walls, sculptural group by Thomas Kirk and richly detailed basilica-plan interior.
candidate_records.appraisal_summary: NIAH identifies it as a major neoclassical building and a focal point of Dublin's Catholic community since its 1825 dedication.
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact registration 50010228 present in workflow #1987 Dublin City missing-registration queue.

candidate_records.name: Pro-Cathedral House
candidate_records.description_summary: Attached four-bay three-storey presbytery over raised basement, built c.1825 in association with the adjacent Pro-Cathedral, with Flemish-bond red brick walls, granite basement, timber sash windows and a decorative Pain-style doorcase.
candidate_records.appraisal_summary: NIAH describes it as a fine early nineteenth-century townhouse with social significance connected to the changing role of the Catholic population.
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact registration 50010229 present in workflow #1987 Dublin City missing-registration queue.

candidate_records.description_summary: Terraced two-bay four-storey house over raised basement, built c.1800, with Flemish-bond red brick walls, timber sliding sash windows, basement iron grille and a round-headed entrance within a tooled limestone doorcase with Doric pilasters.
candidate_records.appraisal_summary: NIAH describes it as a fine Georgian red-brick townhouse with a restrained façade and elegant doorcase.
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact registration 50010231 present in workflow #1987 Dublin City missing-registration queue.

duplicate_screen.method: Exact registration-number search in the workflow-generated official register audit and exact-number searches of repository issues and all pull-request states.
duplicate_screen.result: No archive-register matches and no repository issue or pull-request matches were returned for these five exact registration numbers at time of research.

identity_and_spatial_cautions: All five are distinct NIAH registrations and must remain separate archive building entities.
50010227 is one of the pair of gate lodges at the former National Model Schools campus; 50010220 is its separately registered counterpart. Do not merge the pair.

50010226 retains the national CSV NAME Central Model School, while its NIAH survey describes the building as a former chapel and records original use Church/chapel and current survey use Office. Preserve the distinct source fields rather than resolving the apparent naming/use mismatch by inference.
50010228 is Saint Mary's Catholic Pro-Cathedral; 50010229 is Pro-Cathedral House at 83 Marlborough Street. Their association does not make them one building record.
The national CSV NAME field is blank for 50010227 and 50010231. Do not invent names.
NIAH use, condition and historical descriptions are survey-time statements and do not establish present-day tenant, occupancy, public access or condition.
Raw page coordinate pairs are stored separately from official CSV ITM and latitude/longitude; do not mix coordinate systems.
explicitly_not_done: No source registry or visual inventory imports
No map pins or coordinate imports
